policy_evidence.text: For each binary tag, the replacement-panel analysis will use nominal distance. Additional prevalence-sensitive diagnostics are defined in Section 8.4, and the two tags will be analysed separately.
For each tag: raw, positive, and negative agreement; prevalence; Cohen's kappa; Gwet's AC1; precision; recall; and F1, reported separately for the random baseline and hard-case sample.

Taxonomy fit: individual and record-level majority ratings of Fit, Partial Fit, No Fit and Cannot assess from register entry. Cannot assess will be reported separately as an evidence-sufficiency outcome and will not be counted as No Fit, as a taxonomy defect, or in taxonomy-issue denominators. Taxonomy-issue frequencies will be reported among responses coded Partial Fit or No Fit.

A label's support is the number of random-baseline records human-supported under the two-of-three majority rule. The hard-case sample is excluded from support counts and per-label performance estimation because it is disagreement-enriched.

Fewer than 10 positive records: report human-supported and production-model positive counts, contingency counts, prevalence, examples, and adjudicated issue notes. Cohen's kappa, precision, recall, and F1 will not be presented as per-label performance estimates, and the label will not be included in macro-averages. Contingency quantities may still be calculated internally to support descriptive counts and case diagnostics.
10 to 29 positive records: report per-label metrics with bootstrap intervals and an explicit low-support caution; do not quote point estimates without intervals.

Anticipated support distribution. Using production-model prevalence across the full register as a planning proxy, approximately four of the 22 domain, purpose and tag labels are clearly expected to have at least 30 majority-supported baseline records. Approximately two are clearly expected to fall between 10 and 29, and six are clearly expected to remain below 10. The remaining ten labels lie sufficiently close to either the 10- or 30-record threshold that their reporting band cannot be determined in advance. On point expectations alone, the corresponding split is four labels at 30 or more, seven at 10–29, and eleven below 10. The COVID-19 / pandemic tag is expected to have about nine positive baseline records. Its binary-tag diagnostics, including any tag-level alpha, will therefore be reported descriptively with an explicit low-prevalence caution rather than interpreted as a stable performance estimate. These projections are descriptive planning aids only; the reporting rule will be applied using observed two-of-three human-majority support in the random baseline.

Baseline proportions will use 95% Wilson score intervals. Agreement metrics, replacement differences, delta_min, and eligible per-label metrics will use 2,000 nonparametric record-level bootstrap resamples with percentile intervals and SEED_BOOTSTRAP = 20260714. Percentiles and percentile bootstrap interval endpoints use Hyndman–Fan Type 7 interpolation, equivalent to NumPy/Pandas linear quantile interpolation where those implementations are used. All ratings for a record remain together, and alpha_ABC, all replacement alphas, differences, and delta_min are recalculated jointly within each resample.
